name: External Auditory Canal Aplasia/Hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for External Auditory Canal Aplasia/Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Complete absence of the external auditory canal on clinical examination
Narrowed or underdeveloped external auditory canal visualized on otoscopy or imaging
Associated middle ear ossicular chain anomalies detected by imaging
Presence of conductive hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
CT scan demonstrating aplasia or hypoplasia of the external auditory canal

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent or hypoplastic external auditory canal confirmed clinically and radiologically, along with conductive hearing loss
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by audiometric and imaging studies; differentiation from acquired canal stenosis is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete absence of external auditory canal
Conductive hearing loss due to canal aplasia/hypoplasia
searchTerms: hearing loss from missing ear canal
conductive deafness due to canal underdevelopment
blocked ear canal causing hearing problems

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or markedly narrowed external auditory canal on otoscopic exam
searchTerms: very narrow or missing ear canal seen on exam
absent or tiny ear canal on otoscopy
ear canal not visible or very small
ear canal problem on one side only
unilateral ear canal absence or narrowing

common.symptomName: Speech delay secondary to hearing impairment
searchTerms: late talking due to hearing impairment

common.symptomName: Recurrent otitis media due to anatomical abnormalities
searchTerms: repeated middle ear infections from ear structure
chronic ear infections due to anatomy
frequent ear infections linked to ear canal issues
small ear canals on both sides

occasional.symptomName: Mild sensorineural hearing loss in addition to conductive loss
searchTerms: mild nerve-related hearing loss plus conductive loss
sensorineural hearing loss along with ear canal problems

imaging: CT scan showing absence or hypoplasia of external auditory canal
Imaging evidence of ossicular chain malformations
MRI to assess facial nerve and inner ear structures if indicated
other: Audiometric confirmation of conductive hearing loss
Clinical otoscopic examination revealing canal aplasia or hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of narrowed but patent external auditory canal
No complete canal absence on imaging
History of trauma, infection, or inflammation
Progressive canal narrowing rather than congenital absence
Presence of scarring or debris in canal

redFlags: Complete bilateral external auditory canal aplasia with profound hearing loss
Associated craniofacial anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
